title: Linux sandbox: bwrap binds every WritePath with --bind, which fails the launch when a declared write dir does not exist yet (--bind-try or mkdir-before-bind)
problem: internal/adapters/sandbox/sandbox.go (BwrapPrefix) emits `--bind wp wp` for every WritePath but `--bind-try` for the home state dirs. bwrap's --bind requires the source to exist, so a write grant for a directory that is created lazily by the phase itself — .evolve/instincts/lessons on a fresh repo, .evolve/inbox/processing before the first claim, a profile's docs/ or knowledge-base/ — fails the whole launch on Linux instead of granting the path. macOS SBPL grants a not-yet-existing subpath fine, so the divergence is platform-specific and invisible on the darwin runtime. Pre-existing: the retrospective lesson grant had the same shape before sandbox.write_subpaths was honored; honoring the declarations widens the set of grants that can hit it.
impact: Linux-only launch failures for phases whose declared write dir is created lazily; the repo documents bwrap as a supported backend (runtime-reference.md) but the darwin runtime never exercises it, so this would surface only on a Linux operator or CI host.
fix: Either emit --bind-try for WritePaths whose source does not exist at wrap time (fail-open on the grant, which is the SBPL behavior), or create the directory before binding when it lies under RepoRoot/Workspace. Pin with a BwrapPrefix test over a nonexistent WritePath. Do not add a flag.
acceptance: GenerateBwrapArgv/BwrapPrefix over a WritePath that does not exist produces an argv bwrap accepts (unit test; no bwrap binary needed).
The existing home-state --bind-try behavior is unchanged (regression pin).
notes: Surfaced by the architecture review of the write_subpaths landing (2026-09-12); out of that slice's scope because it is adapter behavior on a platform the runtime does not run.
